# #418 — PROV-9: hook entrypoints as console scripts

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-07-25T23:36:38Z
Updated: 2026-07-25T23:37:27Z

---

Part of #409.

Port the hook entrypoints as console scripts: `ob-memory-provider`, `ob-claude-hook`, `ob-guard`, plus takeover/turn-capture/qmd-startup behavior.

`~/.claude/settings.json` hooks are `"type": "command"` - arbitrary shell. TypeScript was never required; a `bun run <hash-path>` invocation becomes a console script name with no path in it.

## Scope
- Thin entrypoints only: parse stdin, call the domain, render output. Logic lives in importable, testable functions (`CODING_STANDARDS.md`: *"keep script entrypoints thin"*).
- Console scripts declared in `pyproject.toml`.

## Acceptance
- Each entrypoint is exercised by a functional test over stdin to stdout/stderr/exit code.
- No business logic in an entrypoint module (each stays small; the test suite exercises the domain functions directly).
- Hook output shape is byte-compatible with what Claude Code expects today, proven by a test against captured real input.

## Non-goals
Editing `settings.json` - that is PROV-11.
